en: So as to be generally favored or accepted by the people.
Commonly.

popularly.ety:
Etymology tree
English popular
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English popularly
From popular + -ly.

ex.en: The bridge is popularly known as the "Golden Gate."
ex.ja: その橋は一般に「ゴールデンゲート」と呼ばれている。

note.ja: popular + -ly。「一般に・俗に」。

en: Containing an explicit depiction of sexual activity.

pornographic.ety:

English pornographic
From pornography + -ic.

ex.en: There is also a tendency to call "L'Auberge Espagnole" a pornographic film.
ex.ja: 『スパニッシュ・アパートメント』はポルノ映画だ、と主張する向きもある。

note.ja: pornography + -ic。「ポルノの」。

en: A group or company of people, originally especially one having hostile intent; a throng, a crowd.
A group of people summoned to help law enforcement.

ex.en: The sheriff formed a posse to catch the outlaws.
ex.ja: 保安官は無法者を捕らえるために捜索隊を組織した。

note.ja: ラテン語 posse comitatus（州の武力）の短縮。posse は「できること・力」。possible と同じ。

en: The process of transferring heat from an object in order to cool it.
The process of preserving something by cooling.

ex.en: Milk needs refrigeration.
ex.ja: 牛乳は冷蔵が必要だ。

note.ja: refrigerate（冷蔵する）+ -ion。re + frigus（寒さ）。「冷蔵」。refrigerator と同じ。

en: Tending to rouse aversion or to repulse; disgusting.
Having the capacity to repel.

repulsive.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French repulsif, from Medieval Latin repulsivus, from Latin repulsus. By surface analysis, repuls(e) + -ive.
Compare typologically Polish odpychający (< pchnąć), Russian отта́лкивающий (ottálkivajuščij) (< толкну́ть (tolknútʹ)).

ex.en: Death, in whatever form, is repulsive.
ex.ja: 死が、どんな形であれ、おぞましいものです。

note.ja: repulse（撃退する）+ -ive。re + pellere（追い払う）。「嫌悪感を起こさせる」。repel と同じ pel。

en: A brief interval of rest or relief.
A reprieve, especially from a sentence of death.
To delay or postpone (an event).
To allow (a person) extra time to fulfil some obligation.

respite.ety: From Anglo-Norman and Old French respit (“rest”), from Latin respectus. Doublet of respect.

ex.en: The rain gave us a brief respite from the heat.
ex.ja: 雨で暑さからつかの間解放された。

note.ja: ラテン語 respectus（顧慮・猶予）から。respect と同じ語源。「一時的な休息」。

en: Delighting in or feeling pleasure from the pain or humiliation of others.
Of behaviour which takes pleasure in the pain or humiliation of others.

sadistic.ety:
Etymology tree
English sadist
Proto-Indo-European *-ikos
Proto-Italic *-ikos
Latin -icuslbor.
Old French -iquebor.
Middle English -ik
English -ic
English sadistic
From sadist + -ic.

ex.en: The villain in the story is sadistic.
ex.ja: その物語の悪役は残酷だ。

note.ja: sadism + -tic。フランスの作家サド侯爵（Marquis de Sade）の名から。「残酷な」。

en: A Brazilian ballroom dance or dance style.
A Brazilian musical genre, to which the aforementioned dance is danced, which has its roots in West Africa via the slave trade.
To dance the samba.

samba.ety:
Etymology tree
Kongo sembabor.?
Brazilian Portuguese sambabor.
English samba
Borrowed from Brazilian Portuguese samba, possibly borrowed from Kongo semba. Doublet of semba.

ex.en: Samba is a Brazilian rhythm, isn't it?
ex.ja: サンバはブラジルのリズムですね。

ex.en: The waltz and the samba are dances.
ex.ja: ワルツとサンバは踊りです。

note.ja: ポルトガル語 samba から。アフリカの言葉に由来するとされる。

en: Having long, thick, and uncombed hair, fur or wool.
Having a surface like shaggy hair; with a rough nap.

shaggy.ety:
Etymology tree
Old English sċeacga
Middle English *schagge
English shag
Proto-Indo-European *-kos

Proto-West Germanic *-g

Middle English -y
English -y
English shaggy
From shag + -y.

ex.en: They have a big shaggy dog.
ex.ja: 彼らは毛むくじゃらの大きな犬を飼っている。

note.ja: shag（もじゃもじゃの毛）+ -y。「毛むくじゃらの」。

en: Someone who sits, e.g. for a portrait.
One employed to watch or tend something; a babysitter, housesitter, petsitter, etc.

sitter.ety: From Middle English sitter, sittere, syttare, equivalent to sit + -er.

ex.en: We need a sitter for Saturday night.
ex.ja: 土曜の夜にベビーシッターが必要だ。

note.ja: sit + -er。「ベビーシッター（babysitter）・（絵の）モデル」。

en: A slope; an incline, inclination.
A sloped surface or line.
To lean, tilt or incline.
To bias or skew.
Sloping; oblique; slanted.

slant.ety: Late Middle English, from a variant of the earlier form dialectal slent, from Old Norse or another North Germanic source, cognate with Old Norse slent, Swedish slinta (“to slip”), Norwegian slenta (“to fall on the side”), from Proto-Germanic *slintaną. Probably influenced by aslant.

ex.en: When is the slant-eyed geezer coming?
ex.ja: つり目のおじさんはいつ来るの？

note.ja: 北欧語に由来するとされる。「傾斜」→ 偏った「観点」。

en: Characterized by an absence of sleep: wakeful.

sleepless.ety: From Middle English slepeles, from Old English slǣplēas; equivalent to sleep + -less.

ex.en: Tom spent a sleepless night thinking of Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーのことを考えて眠れない夜を過ごした。

ex.en: The affair cost me many sleepless nights.
ex.ja: その件が気掛かりで、私は何日も眠れない夜を過ごさなければならなかった。

ex.en: He was pale with fatigue after his sleepless night.
ex.ja: 夜眠れなくて彼は疲労して顔色が悪かった。

note.ja: sleep + -less。「眠れない」。Sleepless in Seattle。

en: An insult or slight, especially one that is muttered incoherently under one's breath.
An extremely offensive and socially unacceptable term targeted at a group of people (such as an ethnicity, sexual orientation, etc.).
To insult or slight.
To run together; to articulate poorly.

slur.ety:
From Middle English sloor (“thin or fluid mud”). The ultimate origin is uncertain, but perhaps related to a group of words derived from Proto-Germanic *slūm- (“loose, slack, flabby”), such as slumber.
Cognate with Middle Low German sluren (“to trail in mud”). Also related to dialectal Norwegian sløra (“to be careless, to scamp, dawdle”), Danish sløre (“to wobble, be loose”) (especially for wheels); compare Old Norse slóðra (“to drag oneself along”).
* (derogatory term): Influenced by various compounds of sense 1 such as racial slur, ethnic slur, etc.

ex.en: He was drunk and slurring his words.
ex.ja: 彼は酔っ払ってだみ声になっていた。

note.ja: 中英語 sloor（泥）から。「泥を塗る」→「中傷」、音楽で音を「つなげる」→ 不明瞭に発音する。

en: A ball of snow, usually one made in the hand and thrown for amusement in a snowball fight; also a larger ball of snow made by rolling a s…
A cocktail made from lemonade and advocaat.
Of something with rapid growth, often uncontrolled. Compare snowball effect.
To rapidly grow out of proportion or control, from an initially smaller state.
To play at throwing snowballs.

snowball.ety: From Middle English snoweball, snoweballe, snaweballe, snayballe, equivalent to snow + ball. Cognate with Scots snawbaw, German Schneeball, Luxembourgish Schnéiball, Dutch sneeuwbal, Afrikaans sneeubal, Limburgish snieëbal, West Frisian sniebal, Saterland Frisian Sneebaal, Sneebal, Swedish snöboll, Elfdalian sniųoboll, Danish snebold, Norwegian Bokmål snøball, Norwegian Nynorsk snøball and Icelandic snjóbolti.

ex.en: Tom and Mary threw snowballs at each other.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは互いに雪玉を投げ合った。

ex.en: The children were rolling a big snowball.
ex.ja: 子供たちが大きな雪の玉を転がしていた。

ex.en: Tom threw a snowball at Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーに雪玉を投げた。

note.ja: snow + ball。「雪玉」→ 転がるほど大きくなる →「雪だるま式に増える」。

en: To restore to ease, comfort, or tranquility; relieve; calm; quiet; refresh.
To allay; assuage; mitigate; soften.

soothe.ety:
From Middle English sothen (“to verify, prove the validity of”), from Old English sōþian (“to verify, prove, confirm, bear witness to”), from Proto-West Germanic *sanþōn, from Proto-Germanic *sanþōną (“to prove, certify, acknowledge, testify”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁es- (“to be”). Cognate with Danish sande (“to verify”), Swedish sanna (“to verify”), Icelandic sanna (“to verify”). See also sooth. Displaced Old English frēfran, ġefrēfran (“to comfort, console, soothe”), and partially displaced Old English stillan, ġestillan (“to calm, become calm, pacify, quieten”) (whence modern still).
T

ex.en: He tried to soothe the angry man.
ex.ja: 彼は怒っている男をなだめようとした。

ex.en: The nurse soothed the crying child.
ex.ja: 看護婦は泣く子をなだめた。

ex.en: I tried to soothe the child.
ex.ja: 私はその子をなだめようとした。

note.ja: 古英語 sōthian（真実と証明する）から。sooth（真実）。「同意して安心させる」→「なだめる」。

en: A line that is tangent to the velocity of flow of a fluid; equivalent to the path of a specific particle in that flow.
On a weather chart, a line that is tangent to the flow of the wind.
To design and construct the contours of a vehicle etc. so as to offer the least resistance to its flow through a fluid.
To simplify or organize a process in order to increase its efficiency.

From stream + line.

ex.en: From now on I want to attempt to streamline management.
ex.ja: これからは経営の合理化を図りたいと思います。

note.ja: stream（流れ）+ line（線）。「流線」→「流線型にする」→「合理化する」。streamlined と同じ。

en: A large spoon, used for eating food from a bowl.
A spoon too large for eating, usually used for cooking or serving.

tablespoon.ety:
Etymology tree
Middle English table
English table
English spoon
English tablespoon
From table + spoon.

ex.en: Teaspoons? I thought you said tablespoons.
ex.ja: 小さじ？大さじって言わなかった？

note.ja: table + spoon。「食卓用のスプーン」→「大さじ」。

en: Of a substance, slightly sticky.

ex.en: Because he thought Fred's comment was tacky, Larry got up on his high horse.
ex.ja: フレッドの意見がしゃくにさわったラリーは、居丈高な態度に出た。

note.ja: 「べとべとした」は tack（粘着性）+ -y。「安っぽい」は19世紀の tacky（やせ馬）からで別語とされる。

en: The act of one who tampers.

ex.en: He was accused of tampering with evidence.
ex.ja: 彼は証拠を改ざんした疑いをかけられた。

note.ja: tamper（いじくる）+ -ing。temper の変化形。「不正操作・改ざん」。

en: The end or final point of something.
The end point of a transportation system, or the town or city in which it is located.

Learned borrowing from Latin terminus (“boundary, limit”). Doublet of term, Terminus, and termon.

ex.en: The bus terminus is near the station.
ex.ja: バスの終点は駅の近くにある。

note.ja: ラテン語 terminus（境界・終わり）から。→「終点・終着駅」。terminal と同じ。

en: A testis: the male sex and endocrine gland, found in most types of animals, that produces sperm and male sex hormones, including the ster…
Either half of the structure that contains the testes: one side of the scrotum and its contents, considered as one object (one half of th…

testicle.ety: Borrowed from Latin testiculus, diminutive of testis.

ex.en: My hamster has a swollen testicle on one side.
ex.ja: ハムスターの金玉が片方肥大しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 testiculus（小さな睾丸）から。testis（証人・睾丸）。testify と同じ語とされる。

en: To gradually cause (something frozen, such as earth, ice, or snow) to melt or soften by raising the temperature.
To gradually cause (someone or something that is very cold) to warm up.
A gradual melting or softening of something frozen (such as earth, ice, or snow) when the temperature rises; the transformation of someth…
A gradual warming up of someone or something that is very cold.

thaw.ety:
The verb is derived from Middle English thawen, thowen (“to melt (ice, snow, etc.), thaw”), from Old English þāwian, *þāwan (“to thaw”), from Proto-West Germanic *þauwjan (“to melt, thaw; to digest; to dissolve”), from Proto-Germanic *þawjaną (“to thaw”), from Proto-Indo-European *teh₂- (“to melt; to flow, stream”).
The noun is derived from Late Middle English thawe, thowe (“melting of ice, snow, etc., thawing”), from thawen, thowen (verb) (see above).
cognates
* Dutch dooien (“to thaw”)
* German tauen (“to thaw”)
* German Low German deien (“to thaw”)
* Icelandic þeyja (“to thaw”)
* Saterland

ex.en: Make sure to thaw the chicken before cooking.
ex.ja: 鶏肉は調理前に必ず解凍してください。

ex.en: Make sure to thaw the chicken out before cooking.
ex.ja: 鶏肉は調理前に必ず解凍してください。

ex.en: Make sure to thaw out the chicken before cooking.
ex.ja: 鶏肉は調理前に必ず解凍してください。

note.ja: 古英語 thawian（解ける）から。「解ける」→（関係が）和らぐ。

en: The rate at which data is transferred through a system.
The rate of production; the rate at which something can be processed.

throughput.ety: From through + put (after input and output).

ex.en: The new machine doubled the factory's throughput.
ex.ja: 新しい機械で工場の処理量が２倍になった。

note.ja: through（通して）+ put（出す）。「処理量」。input、output と同じ作り。

en: Between or beyond national boundaries.
Involving several nations or nationalities.
Someone operating in several countries.

From trans- + national.

ex.en: Climate change is a transnational problem.
ex.ja: 気候変動は国境を越えた問題だ。

note.ja: trans（越えて）+ national。「国境を越えた」。

en: A three-legged stand or mount.
An organism with three limbs.
To enter the tripod position showing signs of exhaustion or distress.
Of a lizard, to raise its body upright bracing itself on hind legs and tail.

tripod.ety:
PIE word
 *tréyes
Borrowed from Latin tripod- (stem of tripūs, tripodis), from Ancient Greek τρίποδ- (trípod-, stem of τρίπους, τρίποδος (trípous, trípodos), literally “three-footed”); equivalent to tri- + -pod. Doublet of tripus, tripos, and teapoy.

ex.en: Use a tripod to keep the camera steady.
ex.ja: カメラを安定させるために三脚を使いなさい。

note.ja: tri（3）+ pod（足）。3本の足 →「三脚」。

en: A type of flowering plant, genus Tulipa.
The flower of this plant.

tulip.ety: From Middle French tulipe, from earlier tulipan, from Ottoman Turkish دلبند (tülbent, dülbent, “cheesecloth”), from Classical Persian دلبند (dulband, “turban”). Doublet of turban.

ex.en: The tulips have begun to come up.
ex.ja: チューリップが芽を出し始めた。

ex.en: The tulips in my garden are now at their best.
ex.ja: 私の庭のチューリップは今真っ盛りだ。

ex.en: Tulips will be in flower soon.
ex.ja: チューリップはまもなく咲く。

note.ja: トルコ語 tülbent（ターバン）から。花の形がターバンに似ていることから。turban と同じ語源。

en: A frame consisting of two bars crossing each other at right angles and turning on a post or pin, to hinder the passage of animals, but ad…
A gate or bar set across a road to stop carriages, animals, and sometimes people, until a toll is paid.
To form (a road, etc.) in the manner of a turnpike road, or into a rounded form, as the path of a road.

turnpike.ety: From Middle English turnpyke (“spiked barrier across a road”), originally used to block access to such a road until a toll was paid. Equivalent to modern turn + pike (“shaft”).

ex.en: We took the turnpike to save time.
ex.ja: 時間を節約するために有料高速道路を使った。

note.ja: turn（回る）+ pike（槍）。昔の通行料の関所にあった回転式の槍柵から「有料道路」。

en: Not attended; without persons present.
Not attended to; not receiving attention.

unattended.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Germanic *un-
Proto-West Germanic *un-
Old English un-
Middle English un-
English un-
English attended
English unattended
From un- + attended.

ex.en: Mary blamed Jack for leaving their children unattended.
ex.ja: メアリーは子供たちをほったらかしにしていることでジャックを非難した。

ex.en: Our trip was unattended by adventures.
ex.ja: 我々の旅には異常な出来事はなかった。

note.ja: un（否定）+ attended（付き添われた）。「放置された」。

en: That cannot be beaten, defeated or overcome
Someone or something that cannot be beaten.

unbeatable.ety: From un- + beat + -able. Beatable is a back-formation.

ex.en: The other team has an unbeatable defense.
ex.ja: 相手チームは鉄壁の守りを固めている。

note.ja: un（否定）+ beat（負かす）+ -able。「無敵の」。

zh: 承辦殯葬者 /承办殡葬者

A person receiving land in Ireland during the Elizabethan era, so named because they gave an undertaking to abide by several conditions r…

en: Any of several carrion-eating birds of the families Accipitridae and Cathartidae.
A person who profits from the suffering of others.
To circle around one's target as if one were a vulture.

vulture.ety: Borrowed into Middle English from Anglo-Norman vultur, from Old French voutoir, voutre, from Latin vultur, voltur. Displaced native Old English ūf.

ex.en: A vulture circled above the desert.
ex.ja: ハゲワシが砂漠の上空を旋回していた。

note.ja: ラテン語 vultur（ハゲワシ）から。「ハゲワシ」→ 人の不幸で儲ける人。

en: Goods or services that are for sale.

ex.en: He had to reduce the price of his wares.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の品物の値段を下げねばならなかった。

note.ja: 古英語 waru（商品）から。software、hardware の -ware と同じ。「商品」。

en: An expression of approval; praise.
A special acknowledgment; an award.
To embrace or kiss in salutation.
To confer a knighthood on.

accolade.ety: First use appears c. 1591 in the publications of Thomas Lodge, borrowed from French accolade, from Occitan acolada (“an embrace”), from acolar (“to embrace”), from Italian accollato, via Vulgar Latin *accollō (“to hug around the neck”), from Latin ad- + collum (“neck”) (English collar) + -āta.

ex.en: The film received many accolades.
ex.ja: その映画は数々の称賛を受けた。

Containing or abounding in anecdotes.

ex.en: The evidence is only anecdotal.
ex.ja: その証拠は個人の体験談にすぎない。

note.ja: anecdote（逸話）+ -al。ギリシャ語 anekdota（公表されていないもの）。「逸話的な・事例に基づく」。

en: A medical condition in which the capacity of the blood to transport oxygen to the tissues is reduced, either because of too few red blood…
A disease or condition that has anemia as a symptom.

anemia.ety: From Ancient Greek ἀναιμία (anaimía), from ἀν- (an-, “not”) + αἷμα (haîma, “blood”) -ία (-ía). By surface analysis, an- + -emia.

ex.en: The doctor analyzed the blood sample for anemia.
ex.ja: 医者は貧血の検査をするためサンプルを分析した。

ex.en: I collapsed from anemia.
ex.ja: 貧血で倒れました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 an（否定）+ haima（血）。「血がない」→「貧血」。hemoglobin と同じ hem。

en: Violent hatred leading to active opposition; active enmity; energetic dislike.

animosity.ety: From French animosité, from Latin animositas (“courage, spirit, vehemence”), from animosus, from animus (“courage, spirit, mind”); see animose, animate.

ex.en: Then that animosity is being passed on down to us?
ex.ja: じゃあ僕らはその腹いせ受け続けるんですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 animositas（勇気・激しさ）から。animus（心・気性）。「激しい気性」→「敵意」。animal、animate と同じ anim。

en: A medieval primitive cannon, used chiefly in sieges for throwing heavy stone balls.
A bombardon.
To continuously attack something with bombs, artillery shells or other missiles or projectiles.
To attack something or someone by directing objects at them.

bombard.ety:
From Middle English bombard, from Middle French bombarde (“a bombard, mortar, catapult"; also "a bassoon-like musical instrument”), from Latin bombus (“buzzing; booming”).
The modern pronunciation is from modern French bombarde.

ex.en: The teacher began to bombard me with questions.
ex.ja: 先生は僕を質問攻めにし始めたんだ。

ex.en: Sorry for bombarding you with so many questions.
ex.ja: 質問攻めにしてすみませんでした。

note.ja: bombard（昔の大砲）から。ギリシャ語 bombos（ブンという音）。bomb と同じ。「砲撃する」→「質問を浴びせる」。

en: Easily bounced.
Lively, exuberant, energetic.
An excessively bouncing pitch in kickball.

bouncy.ety:
Etymology tree
English bounce
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English bouncy
From bounce + -y.

ex.en: The children jumped on a bouncy castle.
ex.ja: 子どもたちはふわふわ遊具の上で跳びはねた。

note.ja: bounce + -y。「弾む・元気な」。

en: Measured

ex.en: The instruments are carefully calibrated.
ex.ja: その計器は注意深く較正されている。

note.ja: calibrate（目盛りを合わせる）+ -ed。caliber（口径）から。「較正された」。

en: A water bottle, flask, or other vessel, typically used by a soldier or camper as a bottle for carrying water or liquor for drink.
A military mess kit.

canteen.ety: Borrowed from French cantine, itself borrowed from Italian cantina. Doublet of cantina.

ex.en: There is little water left in the canteen.
ex.ja: 水筒にはほとんど水が残っていない。

ex.en: I'm tired of the food in the school canteen.
ex.ja: 学食は飽きちゃった。

ex.en: I'm completely fed up with the food in the school canteen!
ex.ja: 学食は飽きちゃった。

note.ja: イタリア語 cantina（ワイン貯蔵室）から。「酒保・食堂」→ 兵士の「水筒」。

en: An electronic component capable of storing electrical energy in an electric field; especially one consisting of two conductors separated …

capacitor.ety:
From capacity + -or.
Capacitor replaced the term condenser (coined by Alessandro Volta in 1782) to disambiguate it from steam condenser. The coiner is unknown but the change was recommended in 1926 by British Standard Glossary of Terms in Electrical Engineering.

ex.en: A capacitor stores electrical energy.
ex.ja: コンデンサーは電気エネルギーをためる。

note.ja: capacity（容量）+ -or。電気をためる容量を持つもの →「コンデンサー」。capture と同じ cap。

en: That captivates; fascinating.
Very beautiful or attractive.

captivating.ety:

Old English -ende

From captivate + -ing.

ex.en: The music was captivating.
ex.ja: 魅惑的な音楽だった。

note.ja: captivate（魅了する）+ -ing。ラテン語 captivus（捕らえられた）。「心をとりこにする」。capture と同じ cap。

en: Of, pertaining to, or advocating centrism.
A person who advocates centrism.

centrist.ety: From French centriste, equivalent to centre + -ist.

ex.en: He is a centrist politician.
ex.ja: 彼は中道派の政治家だ。

note.ja: center + -ist。「中道派」。

en: Any of (at least) seven centres of spiritual energy in or near the body, according to Ayurveda philosophy.
Synonym of hackery.

chakra.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos

Sanskrit चक्र (cakra)lbor.
Hindi चक्र (cakra)bor.
▲
Sanskrit चक्र (cakra)bor.
English chakra
From Hindi चक्र (cakra) and directly from Sanskrit चक्र (cakra, “wheel, disc, cycle”). As a synonym for hackery, either a correction or hypercorrection of that term based on one of its proposed etymologies. Doublet of chakram, charkha, chukker, cycle, cyclus, kike, and wheel.

ex.en: Yoga teachers often talk about chakras.
ex.ja: ヨガの先生はよくチャクラについて話す。

note.ja: サンスクリット語 cakra（輪）から。体内の霊的な中心。wheel、cycle と同じ印欧祖語。

en: A person employed to drive a private motor car or a hired car of executive or luxury class (like a limousine).
The driver of a fire truck.
To be, or act as, a chauffeur (driver of a motor car).
To transport (someone) in a motor vehicle.

ex.ja: 運転手は３時から職務につきます。

ex.en: A chauffeur sat in front.
ex.ja: 前の席に運転手が座っていた。

ex.en: Tom has been working as Mary's chauffeur for years.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーのお抱え運転手として何年もずっと働いている。

note.ja: フランス語 chauffeur（火をたく人）から。chauffer（暖める）。初期の蒸気自動車の火夫 →「お抱え運転手」。

en: To move in circles or through a circuit.
To cause (a person or thing) to move in circles or through a circuit.

circulate.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin circulātus, perfect passive participle of Late Latin circulō (“to make circular, encircle”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), a later collateral form of circulor (“form a circle (of men) around oneself”), from circulus (“a circle”). See also Middle English circulat(e) (“(alchemy) changed by continuous distillation in a closed vessel”).

ex.en: He circulated the letter among the members.
ex.ja: 彼はその手紙を全員に回覧した。

ex.en: Money circulates through the banking system.
ex.ja: 貨幣は銀行制度を通じて流通する。

ex.en: A full description of him has been circulated in every newspaper.
ex.ja: どの新聞にも彼の詳しい人相書きが載った。

note.ja: ラテン語 circulus（小さな円）から。circle と同じ。ぐるぐる回る →「循環する・広まる」。

en: A male member of a clergy; especially, an ordained (male) Christian minister.

From clergy + -man.

ex.ja: その牧師は今週３組の結婚式を行った。

note.ja: clergy（聖職者たち）+ man。clergy はギリシャ語 klēros（くじ・遺産）。

en: Capable of being conceived or imagined.

conceivable.ety: From Middle English conceyvable, equivalent to conceive + -able.

ex.en: We've tried every conceivable method, but absolutely nothing works.
ex.ja: 私たちは考えられる限り全ての方法を試してみたが、全くどれもうまくいかない。

ex.en: It is hardly conceivable to me that he will fail.
ex.ja: 彼が失敗することは私にはまず考えられない。

ex.en: It is conceivable that he knows the rumor.
ex.ja: おそらく彼はその噂を知っているだろう。

note.ja: conceive（思いつく）+ -able。con + capere（取る）。「考えられる」。concept と同じ。

en: To forgive, excuse or overlook (something that is considered morally wrong, offensive, or generally disliked).
To allow, accept or permit (something that is considered morally wrong, offensive, or generally disliked).

condone.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin condōnāre (“to forgive”).

ex.en: We cannot condone such behavior.
ex.ja: そのようなふるまいを容認することはできない。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ don（与える）+ e。（罪を）すっかり与え許す →「大目に見る・容赦する」。

en: overcrowded

ex.en: Your left eye is congested.
ex.ja: あなたの左目は充血していますよ。

ex.en: The expressway was congested with thousands of cars.
ex.ja: 高速道路は何千もの車で渋滞した。

note.ja: congest（詰め込む）+ -ed。ラテン語 congerere（積み上げる）。「混雑した・充血した」。

To ordain as a bishop.

en: That which contaminates; an impurity; foreign matter.

contaminant.ety: Borrowed from French contaminant, present participle of contaminer (“to contaminate”), from Latin contāmināre. By surface analysis, contaminate + -ant.

ex.en: The water was tested for contaminants.
ex.ja: その水は汚染物質がないか検査された。

note.ja: contaminate（汚染する）+ -ant。ラテン語 contaminare（触れて汚す）。contact と同系。

ex.ja: その二つの部屋は隣り合っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 contiguus（接している）から。con + tangere（触れる）。「隣接した」。contact と同じ。

en: A male member of a council, often a city council or town council.

From council + -man.

ex.en: The councilman voted against the plan.
ex.ja: その市議会議員は計画に反対票を投じた。

note.ja: council（議会）+ man。「市議会議員」。

en: A shrub belonging to the section Vaccinium sect. Oxycoccus of the genus Vaccinium.
The edible red berry of that shrub.
Of the intense red colour of a cranberry.
To gather wild cranberries.

cranberry.ety:
Adapted in the 1640s from Dutch Low Saxon or German Low German Kraanbeere, from Kraan m (which means and is cognate with crane) + Beere f (which means and is cognate with berry). Equivalent to cran- + berry.
Via PIE cognate with Polish żurawina, Ukrainian журавли́на (žuravlýna) (akin to жураве́ль (žuravélʹ, “crane”)); Latvian dzērvene < dzērve (“crane”).

ex.en: We had turkey with cranberry sauce.
ex.ja: 私たちはクランベリーソースを添えた七面鳥を食べた。

note.ja: 低地ドイツ語 kraanbere（ツルの実）から。花の形がツル（crane）の首に似ているため。

en: A type of sauce made from milk and eggs (and usually sugar, and sometimes vanilla or other flavourings) and thickened by heat, served hot…
A similar sauce made from milk and cornflour or custard powder (and usually sugar, and sometimes vanilla or other flavourings) and thicke…

ex.en: I had some custard pudding for an afternoon snack.
ex.ja: おやつにプリンを食べた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 crouste（皮）から。もとはパイ皮に入れた料理。crust と同じ語源。

en: In a way that is not only decisive, but also conclusive and final.

definitively.ety:
Etymology tree
English definitive
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English definitively
From definitive + -ly.

ex.en: The question has not been definitively answered.
ex.ja: その疑問にはまだはっきりした答えが出ていない。

note.ja: definitive + -ly。「決定的に」。

en: To make (something) deviate from its original path or position.
To touch the ball, often unwittingly, after a shot or a sharp pass, thereby making it unpredictable for the other players.

deflect.ety: From Latin deflecto, from de- (“away”) + flecto (“to bend”).

ex.en: He tried to deflect attention from his mistake.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の失敗から注意をそらそうとした。

note.ja: ラテン語 deflectere ＝ de（離して）+ flectere（曲げる）。「そらす」。reflect と同じ flect。

en: The act of deliberating, or of weighing and examining the reasons for and against a choice or measure; careful consideration; mature refl…
Careful discussion and examination of the reasons for and against a measure.

deliberation.ety: From Middle English deliberacioun, from Old French deliberation, from Latin deliberātiō. Morphologically deliberate + -ion.

ex.en: He performed his duty with deliberation.
ex.ja: 彼は慎重に義務を遂行した。

ex.en: Factional in-fighting threw a monkey wrench into the deliberations.
ex.ja: 派閥内の抗争が審議に支障をきたしました。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ liber（天秤で量る：ラテン語 libra「天秤」から）+ ation。重さをよく量り比べること →「熟考・審議」。※ liberate（解放する：liber「自由な」）とは別語源。

en: The process of removing constraints, especially government-imposed economic regulation.

deregulation.ety:
Etymology tree

Proto-Indo-European *déh₁
Proto-Italic *dē
Latin dē
Latin dē-der.
English de-
English regulation
English deregulation
From de- + regulation.

ex.en: It is difficult to peg the direction of interest deregulation.
ex.ja: 金利自由化の方向性を一定するのはむずかしいことです。

ex.en: Gas is a little cheaper with self-service, now that deregulation is kicking in.
ex.ja: 規制緩和が進んで、セルフサービスのガソリン給油は値段が少し安くなった。

note.ja: de（取り去る）+ regulation（規制）。「規制緩和」。

en: Deserted and devoid of inhabitants.
Barren and lifeless.
To deprive of inhabitants.
To devastate or lay waste somewhere.

desolate.ety: From Middle English desolat(e). See Etymology 2 and -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.

ex.en: The public square is desolate.
ex.ja: 広場には誰もいない。

ex.en: The town was desolate after the flood.
ex.ja: 洪水の後町は住む人がいなくなった。

ex.en: If one does not have a hobby, his life may be desolate.
ex.ja: 趣味がないと生活があじけないものになるかもしれない。

note.ja: ラテン語 desolare（見捨てる）から。de + solus（ひとりの）。「ひとりにされた」→「荒れ果てた」。sole、solitude と同じ。

en: To eat quickly, greedily, hungrily, or ravenously.
To rapidly destroy, engulf, or lay waste.

devour.ety: Inherited from Middle English devouren, from Old French devorer (Modern French dévorer), from Latin dēvorō, from vorō.

ex.en: When a dog is very hungry, it devours its food.
ex.ja: 犬は空腹の時、えさをがつがつ食べる。

ex.en: The fire devoured the town.
ex.ja: その火事は町を焼き尽くした。

ex.en: Fire devoured the forest.
ex.ja: 炎が森を包み込んだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 devorare（飲み込む）から。de + vorare（むさぼる）。carnivore（肉食動物）と同じ vor。

en: A large piece of machinery that digs holes or trenches.
A tool for digging.

digger.ety:
From Middle English dyggar, equivalent to dig + -er.
In the sense of "Australian soldier", attributed to the considerable time that soldiers spent digging trenches during World War I.

ex.en: A digger cleared the ground for the new house.
ex.ja: 掘削機が新しい家のために土地をならした。

note.ja: dig + -er。「掘る人・掘削機」。

en: The reduction or the abolition of the military forces and armaments of a nation, and of its capability to wage war.
The act of disarming an opponent in a fight.

disarmament.ety: From disarm + -ment, modeled after armament. By surface analysis, dis + armament.

ex.en: Disarmament is in practice difficult in many countries.
ex.ja: 多くの国において軍備縮小は実際には難しい。

ex.en: Disarmament is sure to make for peace.
ex.ja: 軍縮は必ずや平和に寄与する。

ex.en: The superpowers made significant progress in disarmament.
ex.ja: 軍縮については超大国間で意義深い進展があった。

note.ja: dis（取り去る）+ arm（武器）+ -ament。「武器を取り去ること」→「軍縮」。

en: The characteristic or condition of being dishonest.
An act which is fraudulent or otherwise dishonest.

dishonesty.ety: From Middle English dishoneste (“disgrace, filth”), from Old French deshoneste, equivalent to dis- + honesty or dishonest + -y.

ex.en: I can't answer for his dishonesty.
ex.ja: 私は彼の不正直さの責任を負うことはできない。

ex.en: He charged me with dishonesty.
ex.ja: 彼は私を不正直だと非難した。

ex.en: She charged me with dishonesty.
ex.ja: 彼女は私を不誠実だと非難した。

note.ja: dis（否定）+ honesty（正直）。「不正直」。

en: The state or degree of being divergent: of diverging.
The operator which maps a function F=(F₁, ... Fₙ) from a n-dimensional vector space to itself to the function ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ(∂F_i)/(∂x_i).

ex.en: There is a divergence of opinion within the team.
ex.ja: チーム内で意見が分かれている。

note.ja: diverge（分岐する）+ -ence。di（離れて）+ vergere（傾く）。「分岐・相違」。converge（集まる）の対。

en: Selectively bred to live with or around humans. (of an animal or a plant, especially a pet)

From domesticate + -ed.

ex.en: The animals which live on farms are domesticated.
ex.ja: 牧場で暮らす動物は家畜です。

ex.en: Cats were domesticated by the Egyptians.
ex.ja: ネコはエジプト人によって飼い慣らされたものである。

ex.en: In contrast to the dog, the cat has become domesticated only in recent times.
ex.ja: イヌとは対照的に、ネコはごく最近になって飼いならされたものである。

note.ja: domesticate（飼いならす）+ -ed。ラテン語 domus（家）。「家畜化された」。domestic と同じ。

en: In a double manner; with twice the severity or degree.
In two ways.

doubly.ety: From Middle English dowbly, doubli, dubli, doubeliche, equivalent to double + -ly.

ex.en: Be doubly careful on icy roads.
ex.ja: 凍った道では二重に注意しなさい。

note.ja: double + -ly。「二重に」。

A circular life raft.
To encircle something.

ex.ja: ヨーロッパの主要都市の多くはドーナツ化現象に悩まされている。

note.ja: dough（生地）+ nut（木の実）。もとは木の実のような小さな丸い揚げ菓子だった。

en: The condition of being equivalent or essentially equal: the status of being interchangeable.
An act of equating two things; an assertion of equivalence.
To be equivalent or equal to; to counterbalance.

equivalence.ety: From French équivalence, from Medieval Latin aequivalentia.

ex.en: The test shows the equivalence of the two methods.
ex.ja: その試験は二つの方法が同等であることを示している。

note.ja: equivalent（同等の）+ -ence。aequus（等しい）+ valere（価値がある）。「同等」。equal、value と同じ。

ja: 一部の人にしかわからない

en: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with a specialized knowledge or interest, or an enlightened inne…
Having to do with concepts that are highly theoretical and without obvious practical application; often with mystical or religious connot…
An esoteric doctrine or treatise; esoteric philosophy.
One who believes, or is an initiate, in esoteric doctrines or rites.

esoteric.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek ἐσωτερικός (esōterikós, “belonging to an inner circle”), from ἐσωτέρω (esōtérō, “further inside”), comparative of ἔσω (ésō, “within”), from ἐς (es), εἰς (eis, “into”) (the term esoteric referred originally to the secret teachings of Greek philosophers, versus public or exoteric ones).

ex.en: The book is too esoteric for most readers.
ex.ja: その本はほとんどの読者にとって難解すぎる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 esōterikos（内側の）から。esō（内に）。「内輪の人にしかわからない」→「難解な」。exoteric（一般向けの）の対。

en: The practice of intentionally killing a human being or animal in a humane way, especially in order to end suffering.
The practice of killing a human being who is considered a liability to society, especially a disabled person.

euthanasia.ety: First attested in 1606, from Ancient Greek εὐθανασία (euthanasía), from εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + θάνατος (thánatos, “death”)

ex.en: Euthanasia is legal in some countries.
ex.ja: 安楽死が合法な国もある。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 eu（よい）+ thanatos（死）。「よい死」→「安楽死」。euphoria と同じ eu。

en: Of a person or animal, their actions, thoughts, etc.: brutal, cruel, harsh, heartless; also, evil, wicked.
Of a place: harsh, savage, wild; of a thing: deadly; harmful.
A person who has committed a felony (“a serious criminal offence”); specifically, one who has been tried and convicted of such a crime.

felon.ety:
The adjective is derived from Middle English feloun, felun (“base, wicked; hostile; of an animal: dangerous; of words: angry, harsh, slanderous; of things: dangerous, deadly; false, fraudulent; unlucky”) [and other forms], from Old French felon (“bad, evil, immoral”) (compare fel (“evil; despicable, vile”)), from Early Medieval Latin fellōnem; further etymology uncertain.
Doublet of fell (“of a strong and cruel nature; fierce; grim; ruthless, savage”).
Etymology 1, adjective sense 3 (“obtained through a felony”) is derived from the noun.
The noun is derived from Middle English feloun, felun (“

ex.en: The escaped felon was caught yesterday.
ex.ja: 逃走していた重罪犯が昨日捕まった。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 fello（悪人）から。「重罪犯」。felony（重罪）。

en: Capable of burning.
Easily set on fire.
Any flammable substance.

flammable.ety: Back-formation from inflammable, which is used to avoid confusion with non-flammable, as the prefix in- is often used to mean "un-; non-", although it was originally meant in a sense closely related to en-.

ex.en: Keep flammable materials away from the stove.
ex.ja: 燃えやすいものはコンロから遠ざけなさい。

note.ja: ラテン語 flammare（燃やす）から。「燃えやすい」。inflammable も同じ意味（in は否定でない）なので注意。

en: A hard transparent mineral that is often used as gemstones and abrasives.
A dark red color, like that of the gemstone.
Of a dark red colour.
To shred (twisted wool fiber, rags, etc.) so that it can be reused.

garnet.ety: From Middle English gernet, granate, from Old French grenate, from grenat (“pomegranate red”). Doublet of grenade.

ex.en: She wore a ring with a red garnet.
ex.ja: 彼女は赤いガーネットの付いた指輪をしていた。

note.ja: 中世ラテン語 granatum（ざくろ）から。色と形がざくろの種に似ていることから。grain、pomegranate と同じ。

en: The tree of the species Citrus paradisi, a hybrid of Citrus maxima and sweet orange.
The large spherical tart fruit produced by this tree.

grapefruit.ety: Widely assumed to be a marketing term from grape + fruit, an allusion to the supposed grapelike clusters of fruit on the tree, early 19th c. Ciardi proposes another theory: one of the pomelo's botanical names is Citrus grandis, meaning “great citrus [fruit]”, due to the size of its fruit. A new pomelo variety might first have been called a GRAYT-froot (see greatfruit), and through the process of assimilation, the word came to be pronounced GRAYP-froot.

ex.en: Do you have grapefruit juice?
ex.ja: グレープフルーツジュースはありますか？

ex.en: I don't like grapefruit.
ex.ja: グレープフルーツは嫌いなんだよ。

ex.en: I prefer grapefruits to oranges.
ex.ja: 私はオレンジよりグレープフルーツのほうが好きだな。

note.ja: grape（ぶどう）+ fruit。房になってぶどうのように実ることから。

en: A horizontal metal grill through which liquid, ash, or small objects can fall, while larger objects cannot.
A frame or bed, or kind of basket, of iron bars, for holding fuel while burning.
To furnish with grates; to protect with a grating or crossbars.

grate.ety: From Middle English grate, from a Medieval Latin crāta, from a Latin word for a hurdle; or Italian grata, from Latin cratis.

ex.en: Good advice grates on the ear.
ex.ja: 忠言耳に逆らう。

note.ja: 「すりおろす・きしむ」は古フランス語 grater（引っかく）から。「火格子」はラテン語 cratis（格子）からで別語。

en: A lean breed of dog used in hunting and racing.
A highball cocktail of vodka and grapefruit juice.
Of fish, to leap rapidly across the surface of the water.

greyhound.ety: From Old English grīġhund, from a cognate or borrowing of Old Norse grøy (“bitch”) (whence Icelandic grey, thus not related to the colour grey) plus hund (“hound”). Altered by folk etymology to appear to be grey + hound and so in the form grayhound by analogy.

ex.en: How fast Greyhound buses run!
ex.ja: グレイハウンドバスはなんて速く走るのだろう。

note.ja: 古英語 grīghund から。grey（灰色）との関係ははっきりしない。「猟犬の一種」。

ex.ja: 彼女はいつも有名な美容師に髪を結ってもらう。

note.ja: hair（髪）+ dress（整える）+ -er。「髪を整える人」→「美容師」。dress はもとは「整える」の意味。

en: The quality of being hard.
An instance of this quality; hardship.

hardness.ety: From Middle English hardness, hardnesse, from Old English heardnes, from heard + -nes, equivalent to hard + -ness.

ex.en: The hardness of diamond is such that it can cut glass.
ex.ja: ダイヤモンドの硬度は非常なものなのでガラスが切れます。

ex.en: The hardness of diamond is 10.
ex.ja: ダイヤモンドの硬度は１０である。

ex.en: One of the qualities of steel is hardness.
ex.ja: 鉄鋼の特性の１つは硬いことだ。

note.ja: hard（硬い）+ -ness。「硬さ」。

en: Abundant in hills; having many hills.

hilly.ety: From Middle English hilly, hylly, hully, equivalent to hill + -y.

ex.en: Austria's hilly landscapes reminded Mr. Bogart of The Sound of Music.
ex.ja: オーストリアの山がちな地形を見て、ボガート氏の『サウンド・オブ・ミュージック』を思い出しました。

note.ja: hill + -y。「丘の多い」。

en: A sharpening stone composed of extra-fine grit used for removing the burr or curl from the blade of a razor or some other edge tool.
A machine tool used in the manufacture of precision bores.
To sharpen with a hone; to whet.
To use a hone to produce a precision bore.
Synonym of alas Used to express sorrow, or grief

hone.ety: From Middle English hon (“whetstone”), from Old English hān, from Proto-Germanic *hainō (compare Dutch heen, Norwegian hein), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱeh₃i- (“to sharpen”) (compare Ancient Greek κῶνος (kônos, “cone”), Persian سان (sân, “whetstone”)).

ex.en: She practices every day to hone her skills.
ex.ja: 彼女は技術を磨くために毎日練習している。

note.ja: 古英語 hān（石）から。「砥石」→「研ぐ」→「（技術を）磨く」。

en: In a humble manner.

humbly.ety: From Middle English humbely, humbliche. By surface analysis, humble + -ly. Displaced Old English ēaþmōdlīċe.

ex.en: To be continued next time, and thus I most humbly request your attendance then.
ex.ja: 次回につづく、ということで、どうかお付き合いのほど、平にお願いいたします。

note.ja: humble + -ly。「謙虚に」。

en: To call into action.
To entreat an act.

incite.ety: From Middle French inciter, from Latin incitō (“to set in motion, hasten, urge, incite”), from in (“in, on”) + citō (“to set in motion, urge”), frequentative of cieō (“to rouse, excite, call”).

ex.en: The speaker tried to incite the people to rebellion.
ex.ja: 演説者は民衆をそそのかして反乱を起こさせようとした。

ex.en: They incited him to commit the crime.
ex.ja: 彼らは彼をけしかけてその悪事を働かせた。

ex.en: Shades of earth are ringing through my open view inciting and inviting me.
ex.ja: 大地の色彩は解き放たれた視界の中で高らかに鳴り響き。

note.ja: ラテン語 incitare（駆り立てる）から。in + citare（動かす）。「扇動する」。excite、cite と同じ cit。

en: The property of a body that resists any change to its uniform motion; equivalent to its mass.
In a person, unwillingness to take action.

inertia.ety: From Latin inertia (“lack of art or skill, inactivity, indolence”), from iners (“unskilled, inactive”), from in- (“without, not”) + ars (“skill, art”). Something close to the modern physics sense was first used in New Latin by Johannes Kepler.

ex.en: The company suffers from bureaucratic inertia.
ex.ja: その会社はお役所的な惰性に陥っている。

note.ja: ラテン語 inertia（無技能・怠惰）から。in（否定）+ ars（技術）。「動かない」→「慣性・惰性」。inert と同じ。art と同じ語根。

en: The presence of a large number of pest organisms in an area or field, on the surface of a host or anything that might contact a host, or …

infestation.ety: From Middle French infestation, from Late Latin infestatio. Morphologically infest + -ation.

ex.en: The house had an infestation of termites.
ex.ja: その家にはシロアリがはびこっていた。

note.ja: infest（はびこる）+ -ation。ラテン語 infestus（敵意のある）。「（害虫の）発生」。

en: The action of part or all of a national population violently rising up against the government or other authority; (countable) an instance…

insurrection.ety: From Late Middle English insurreccion (“uprising against a government, rebellion, revolt; civil disorder, riot; illegal armed assault”) [and other forms], from Middle French insurrection, Old French insurreccïon (modern French insurrection), and from their etymon Latin īnsurrēctiōnem (rare), the accusative singular of īnsurrēctiō (“rising up, insurrection, rebellion”), from īnsurgō (“to rise up”), from in- (prefix meaning ‘in, inside, within’) + surgō (“to arise, get up; to rise”) (from sub- (prefix meaning ‘(from) beneath, under’) + regō (“to direct, govern, rule; to guide, steer; to manage,

ex.en: The army put down the insurrection.
ex.ja: 軍は反乱を鎮圧した。

note.ja: in（〜に対して）+ sur（下から上へ）+ rect（まっすぐ）+ ion。立ち上がること →「反乱・暴動」。resurrection（再び立ち上がる→復活）と同じ構造。

zh: 难以忍受的,難以忍受的

en: Not tolerable; not capable of being borne or endured.
Extremely offensive or insulting.

intolerable.ety: Inherited from Middle English intolerable, borrowed from Middle French intolerable, from Latin intolerābilis. By surface analysis, in- + tolerable.

ex.en: It drives me insane how intolerable my younger brother is.
ex.ja: 弟がうざすぎて頭おかしくなりそう。

ex.en: The pain from the compound fracture was almost intolerable.
ex.ja: 複雑骨折の痛みはほとんど耐え難かった。

note.ja: in（否定）+ tolerable（耐えられる）。ラテン語 tolerare（耐える）。「耐えられない」。

ex.ja: なまけていては成功しない。

ex.en: I'm fed up with her laziness.
ex.ja: 私は彼女の怠慢さにうんざりしています。

note.ja: lazy（怠惰な）+ -ness。「怠惰」。

en: A typically aquatic blood-sucking annelid of the subclass Hirudinea, especially Hirudo medicinalis.
A person who derives advantage from others in a parasitic fashion.
To apply a leech medicinally, so that it sucks blood from the patient.
To drain (resources) without giving back.

leech.ety: From Middle English leche (“blood-sucking worm”), from Old English lǣċe (“blood-sucking worm”), akin to Middle Dutch lāke ("blood-sucking worm"; > modern Dutch laak).

ex.en: A leech attached itself to my leg in the river.
ex.ja: 川でヒルが私の脚に吸いついた。

note.ja: 古英語 lǣce（ヒル）から。昔は医者の治療に使われた。「ヒル」→ 人の血を吸う「たかり屋」。

en: Without reason or understanding; wildly.
Angrily.

madly.ety: From Middle English madly, madli, medliche, equivalent to mad + -ly.

ex.en: He is madly in love with that girl.
ex.ja: 彼はあの娘に完全に参っている。

ex.en: Joe is madly in love with that girl.
ex.ja: ジョーはその女の子にすっかり参っている。

ex.en: It's true that I was madly in love with her.
ex.ja: 彼女への愛に我を忘れていたのは事実だ。

note.ja: mad + -ly。「狂ったように」→ madly in love（熱烈に恋して）。

en: An arranged informal meeting.

ex.en: We had a meetup for English learners.
ex.ja: 英語学習者の交流会を開いた。

note.ja: meet up（会う）の名詞化。「集まり・交流会」。

en: In a miserable manner.

miserably.ety: From Middle English myserablie; equivalent to miserable + -ly.

ex.en: It was down to her that he lived so miserably.
ex.ja: 彼女のおかげで彼はみじめな暮らしをした。

ex.en: It was because of her that he lived so miserably.
ex.ja: 彼女のおかげで彼はみじめな暮らしをした。

note.ja: miserable（惨めな）+ -ly。ラテン語 miser（哀れな）。「惨めに」。misery と同じ。

en: auto racing
Any sport involving automobiles (motor cars) other than racing; e.g. time trials

ex.en: Formula One is the most famous motorsport.
ex.ja: Ｆ１は最も有名なモータースポーツだ。

note.ja: motor（モーター）+ sport。「モータースポーツ」。

en: The act of mutilating or the state of being mutilated.

ex.en: The law bans the mutilation of animals.
ex.ja: その法律は動物の体を傷つけることを禁じている。

note.ja: mutilate（切断する）+ -ion。ラテン語 mutilus（手足を失った）。「切断・損傷」。

en: A safeguard.

palladium.ety: The sense of "safeguard" comes from Latin Palladium (the image of Pallas that protected Troy), from Ancient Greek Παλλάδιον (Palládion), from Παλλάς (Pallás), an epithet used before Athena.

ex.en: Palladium is used in car parts.
ex.ja: パラジウムは自動車部品に使われている。

note.ja: 小惑星パラス（Pallas）にちなんで名づけられた元素。パラスはギリシャ神話の女神アテナの別名。

zh: 帕馬森起司 /帕马森起司

en: A hard, full-fat Italian cheese from Parma or its neighboring province Reggio Emilia.
A similar cheese produced elsewhere.

parmesan.ety:
Borrowed from Middle French parmesan, from an earlier Vulgar Latin *parmēsānus, restructuring of Latin parmēnsis (from Latin Parma).
Compare Italian parmigiano, Catalan parmesà, Portuguese parmesão, Sicilian parmisanu, Spanish parmesano

ex.en: Do you like Parmesan cheese on spaghetti?
ex.ja: スパゲッティにパルメザンチーズをかけるの好き？

note.ja: イタリアのパルマ（Parma）の。パルマ産のチーズ。

en: Any of various seabirds of the family Pelecanidae, having a long bill with a distendable pouch.
A native or resident of the American state of Louisiana.

pelican.ety:
From Middle English pellican, pellicane, from Old English pellican (“pelican”), from Latin pelecānus, from Ancient Greek πελεκάν (pelekán),
πέλεκυς (pélekus, “hatchet”).

ex.en: I saw a big pelican there.
ex.ja: そこで大きなペリカンを見たよ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pelekan から。pelekys（斧）とされる。くちばしの形からとされる。

zh: 領養老金的人 /领养老金的人

en: Someone who lives on a pension, especially the retirement or old age pension.
Someone who is at the age at which one typically receives a pension; an elderly person.

pensioner.ety: From Middle English pensioner, from Anglo-Norman pensionner and Old French pensionnier, from Medieval Latin pēnsiōnārius. By surface analysis, pension + -er.

ex.en: The pensioner lives alone in a small flat.
ex.ja: その年金生活者は小さなアパートで一人暮らしをしている。

note.ja: pension（年金）+ -er。ラテン語 pensio（支払い）、pendere（量る・支払う）。「年金受給者」。pendant と同じ pend。

en: A public square, especially in Italian cities.
A roofed gallery or arcade (for example around a public square or in front of a building).

piazza.ety: From Italian piazza. Doublet of piatza, place, platz, and plaza.

ex.en: We drank coffee in the piazza.
ex.ja: 私たちは広場でコーヒーを飲んだ。

note.ja: イタリア語 piazza（広場）から。ラテン語 platea（大通り）。place、plaza と同じ語源。

en: Of or pertaining to ownership or possession.
Indicating ownership, possession, origin, etc.
The possessive case.
A word used to indicate the possessive case.

possessive.ety: From Middle French possessif, from Latin possessivus (“of or pertaining to possession”), from possessiō (“possessing”), from possidēre (“to possess”). By surface analysis, possess + -ive.

ex.en: He is very possessive of his toys.
ex.ja: 彼は自分のおもちゃへの独占欲がとても強い。

note.ja: possess + -ive。「独占欲の強い」→ 文法の「所有格」。

en: The office or position of a prefect.
The jurisdiction of a prefect; the region administered by a prefect, especially as a translation of certain French, Chinese, and Japanese…

prefecture.ety: Borrowed from Middle French préfecture, from Latin praefectūra. Equivalent to prefect + -ure. As an East Asian administrative division, a calque of Chinese 府 (fǔ) and 郡 (jùn), also used to describe 縣 /县 (xian, “county”) and 州 (zhou, “province”) in some eras.

ex.en: How many prefectures are there in Japan?
ex.ja: 日本には、県がいくつありますか。

ex.en: How many prefectures does Japan have?
ex.ja: 日本には、都道府県は幾つあるの？

ex.en: Six high-tech companies set up branch offices in that prefecture.
ex.ja: ６つの先端技術の会社がその県に支社を設立した。

en: Motivated by an inappropriate, excessive, or unjustified desire to impress others.
Marked by an unwarranted claim to importance or distinction.

pretentious.ety:
From French prétentieux, from prétention, from Latin praetēnsus (“false or hypocritical profession”), past participle of praetendō.
Note that pretentious is spelled with a ‘t’, unlike related pretense, pretension. This is due to the French spelling: *-sious does not occur as an English suffix, though -sion and -tion both do.

ex.en: Her nature is neither affected nor pretentious.
ex.ja: 彼女の態度は気取りやわざとらしさがない。

note.ja: pretension（見せかけ）+ -ous。ラテン語 praetendere（前に広げる）。「気取った」。pretend と同じ。

en: A prom (dance).
A walk taken for pleasure, display, or exercise; a stroll.
To walk for amusement, show, or exercise.
To perform the stylized walk of a square dance.

promenade.ety: Unadapted borrowing from French promenade, from promener (“to walk”).

ex.en: It is a lovely riverside promenade.
ex.ja: それは川沿いの美しい遊歩道です。

ex.en: The promenade runs parallel to the shore.
ex.ja: 遊歩道は海岸と平行に走っている。

note.ja: フランス語 promener（散歩させる）から。ラテン語 prominare（追い立てる）。「散歩・遊歩道」。

en: Closer to the point of attachment or observation.
Facing toward another tooth. The proximal surfaces of a tooth are those that touch or are close to neighboring teeth.

ex.ja: けがは骨の近位端にあった。

note.ja: ラテン語 proximus（最も近い）から。「（体の中心に）近い側の」。distal の対。approximate と同じ。

en: A relationship of mutual trust and respect; a close and harmonious relationship in which the people or groups concerned understand each o…
Relation; proportion; conformity.

rapport.ety: Borrowed from French rapport. Doublet of report.

ex.ja: その先生は生徒たちとよい信頼関係を築いている。

note.ja: フランス語 rapport（関係）から。rapporter（持ち帰る）、re + ad + portare（運ぶ）。「心の通い合い」。report、transport と同じ port。

en: Extreme pleasure, happiness or excitement.
A spasm; a fit; a syncope; delirium.
To take (someone) off the Earth and bring (them) to Heaven as part of the Rapture.
To state (something, transitive) or talk (intransitive) rapturously.

rapture.ety: Borrowed from Middle French rapture, from Latin raptūra, future active participle of rapiō (“snatch, carry off”).

ex.ja: 聴衆はうっとりと聞き入った。

note.ja: ラテン語 raptus（奪われた）から。rapere（奪う）。「心を奪われること」→「有頂天」。rapid、rape と同じ語源。

en: To devastate, destroy or lay waste to something.
To pillage or plunder destructively; to sack.
Grievous damage or havoc.
Depredation or devastation.

ravage.ety: From French ravage (“ravage, havoc, spoil”), from ravir (“to bear away suddenly”), from Latin rapere (“to snatch, seize”), akin to Ancient Greek ἁρπάζω (harpázō, “to seize”).

ex.en: It often ravages hunters' cabins and steals prey from traps.
ex.ja: しばしば、それは狩人の小屋を壊し、罠から獲物を盗む。

note.ja: フランス語 ravager（荒らす）から。ravir（奪う）、ラテン語 rapere。「荒らす」。ravine と同じ語源。

To meet up again (with someone), after a long time apart and/or without communication; to reunite.

en: To restore (someone or something) to its proper condition; to straighten out, to set right.
To remedy or fix (an undesirable state of affairs, situation etc.).

rectify.ety: From Middle English rectifien, from Anglo-Norman rectifiier, rectefier (“to make straight”), from Medieval Latin rēctificō (“to make right”), from Latin rēctus (“straight”).

ex.ja: その会社は誤りを正すと約束した。

note.ja: rect（まっすぐ）+ ify。まっすぐにする →「正す・是正する」。

One of the rudimentary (adjective sense 1) mammae of boars.

en: A square or rectangular piece of cloth worn as a covering for the head, neck, and shoulders, typically by women.
A fold of wrinkled flesh under the lips and neck of a bloodhound, used in scenting.
To wrap in a shawl.

ex.ja: 彼女は肩にショールを巻いた。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 shāl から。「ショール」。

ex.ja: その本は５シリングだった。

To conceal or hide from view, as if by a shroud.

ex.ja: 霧のとばりが山を覆っていた。

To pass near the surface of; to brush the surface of; to glide swiftly along the surface of.
Having lowered fat content.
A cursory reading, skipping the details.
Skim milk.

skim.ety: From Middle English skemen, skymen, variants of scumen, from Old French escumer (“to remove scum”), from escume (“froth, foam”), from Frankish *skūm (“froth, foam”), from Proto-Germanic *skūmaz (“foam”), from Proto-Indo-European *skew- (“to cover, conceal”). See scum.

ex.en: Please give it a quick skim.
ex.ja: 適当に読み流してください。

ex.ja: 彼は報告書にざっと目を通した。

ex.en: I skimmed through the book.
ex.ja: 私は本にざっと目を通した。

note.ja: 古フランス語 escumer（泡をすくう）から。escume（泡）。scum（浮きかす）と同じ。「すくい取る」→「表面だけざっと読む」。

en: Of, from, or pertaining to Slovakia, the Slovak people or the Slovak language.
A person from Slovakia or of Slovak descent.

Slovak.ety: From Slovak Slovák (“Slovak”), from a shortening of Proto-Slavic *slověninъ (“Slav”) + -ák. Related to Slovene.

ex.en: I can understand Slovak, but I can't speak it.
ex.ja: スロバキア語は分かるんだけど、話せない。

ex.en: "Are you Russian?" "No, I'm Slovak."
ex.ja: 「ロシアの方ですか？」「いいえ、スロバキア人です」

note.ja: スロバキア語 Slovák から。Slav（スラブ人）と同じ語。

ex.ja: その建物では勧誘は禁止されている。

note.ja: solicit（懇願する）+ -ation。ラテン語 sollicitare（揺り動かす）。「勧誘」。solicitor と同じ。

To be bright with delight.
A sparkle or glimmer of light.
A sparkle of delight in the eyes.

twinkle.ety: From Middle English twinclen, twynclen, from Old English twinclian (“to twinkle”), equivalent to twink (“to wink; blink; twinkle”) + -le (frequentative suffix). Compare German zwinkern (“to wink; twinkle”).

ex.en: There was a happy twinkle in her eyes.
ex.ja: 彼女は幸福そうに目を輝かせていた。

ex.en: Many stars are twinkling in the sky.
ex.ja: たくさんの星が空にきらめいている。

ex.en: The stars were twinkling in the sky.
ex.ja: 星が空に瞬いていた。

note.ja: 古英語 twinclian から。擬態的な語。「きらきら光る」。Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star。

A hotel employee performing such duties for guests.

To clean and service (a car), as a valet does.

ex.ja: 従者にとっては誰も英雄ではない。

A bitter, destructive feud, normally between two families, clans, or factions, in which each injury or slaying is revenged: a blood feud.

vendetta.ety: Borrowed from Italian vendetta (“revenge”), from Latin vindicta. See vindicate, avenge.

ex.en: It's like a vendetta now.
ex.ja: これは復讐みたいなもんだ。

note.ja: イタリア語 vendetta（復讐）から。ラテン語 vindicta（報復）。vindicate、vengeance と同じ語源。

en: Frail, sickly or of a delicate constitution; weak.

ex.ja: 彼女は弱々しくほほえんだ。

note.ja: weak + -ly。「弱々しく」。

An uncontrolled or unpredictable element.

note.ja: alienate（疎外する）+ -ion。ラテン語 alienus（他人の）。「よそ者にすること」→「疎外」。alien と同じ。

ex.ja: 医師は抗うつ薬を処方した。

note.ja: anti（対抗）+ depressant（抑うつ）。「抗うつ薬」。

en: Grinding down or wearing away by friction.
The wearing of teeth due to their grinding.
To grind or wear down through friction.
To reduce the number of (jobs or workers) by not hiring new employees to fill positions that become vacant (often with out).

ex.en: The company reduced staff through attrition.
ex.ja: その会社は自然減によって人員を減らした。

en: A rescue, especially a financial rescue.
The process of exiting an aircraft while in flight.

note.ja: bail out（水をくみ出す・救い出す）の名詞化。「（財政的）救済」。

en: Heavy material that is placed in the hold of a ship (or in the gondola of a balloon), to provide stability.

To stabilize or load a ship with ballast.
To lay ballast on the bed of a railroad track.

ex.en: The ship carried rocks as ballast.
ex.ja: その船は底荷として岩を積んでいた。

note.ja: 古北欧語 barlast とされる。bar（むき出しの）+ last（荷）。「底荷」。

biotech.ety: Clipping of biotechnology. Analyzable as bio- (“biological”) + tech (“technology”) or as a clipped compound, bio(logical) tech(nology).

ex.en: She works for a biotech startup.
ex.ja: 彼女はバイオテクノロジーの新興企業で働いている。

note.ja: biotechnology の短縮。

note.ja: cheer（応援する）+ lead（先導する）+ -ing。「チアリーディング」。

en: Any black or brown straight-winged insect of the order Blattodea that is not a termite.

cockroach.ety: From Spanish cucaracha, from cuca (“butterfly caterpillars”), of onomatopoeic origin; see also Greek κόκκυξ (kókkux) and Late Latin cucus. Influenced, by means of folk etymology, by cock and roach. Doublet of cucaracha.

ex.en: I must rid my kitchen of cockroaches.
ex.ja: 台所からゴキブリを駆除しなければならない。

ex.en: It's exciting to watch her run after a cockroach.
ex.ja: 彼女がゴキブリを追いかけるのを見ていると面白い。

ex.en: She's only interested in fish and cockroaches.
ex.ja: 彼女は魚とゴキブリにだけ興味がある。

note.ja: スペイン語 cucaracha から。英語の cock（おんどり）+ roach（魚の一種）に当てはめて変形した。

en: Burdensome or hindering, as if a weight or drag; vexatious.
Not easily managed or handled; awkward or clumsy.

cumbersome.ety: From Middle English cumbyrsum, cummyrsum; equivalent to cumber (“hindrance”) + -some. Compare encumber and incumbent.

ex.en: Transferring to the Keiyō Line from other lines at Tokyo Station is extremely cumbersome.
ex.ja: 東京駅で他の路線から京葉線に乗り換えるのは非常に面倒くさい。

note.ja: cumber（妨げる）+ -some。「扱いにくい」。encumber と同じ。

en: Brief or terse, especially to the point of being rude.
Short or concise.

curt.ety: From the Latin curtus (“shortened”). Cognate with Dutch kort, German kurz, Galician curto, French court, Italian corto, Portuguese curto, and Spanish corto. Doublet of short.

ex.en: He gave me a curt answer.
ex.ja: 彼はけんもほろろな返事をした。

ex.en: Don't you think it's rude to give people such a curt reply like that?
ex.ja: 木で鼻をくくったその返事の仕方、相手に失礼だと思わんのかね。

note.ja: ラテン語 curtus（短く切った）から。「短い」→「そっけない」。short と同系。

en: To take one thing from another; remove from; make smaller or less by some amount.

deduct.ety: Borrowed from Latin deductus, perfect passive participle of verb deducere (“lead from”).

ex.ja: 税金は給料から差し引かれる。

ex.ja: 熱でプラスチックが変形した。

note.ja: deform（変形させる）+ -ation。de + forma（形）。「変形」。form と同じ。

ex.ja: 農家は育てる作物の種類を増やしている。

A duplicate.

ex.ja: エジソンは複写の装置を発明した。

The mechanism by which a celestial body, such as the Earth or a star, generates a magnetic field.

dynamo.ety: A shortening of dynamo-electric machine. The element dynamo- is ultimately from Ancient Greek δύναμις (dúnamis, “power”).

ex.en: She is a dynamo of energy.
ex.ja: 彼女はエネルギーの塊のような人だ。

note.ja: dynamo-electric machine の短縮。ギリシャ語 dynamis（力）。「発電機」→「精力的な人」。dynamic、dynamite と同じ。

en: A liquid which converts lead to gold.
A substance or liquid which is believed to cure all ills and give eternal life.

elixir.ety: From Medieval Latin elixir (“philosopher's stone”), from Arabic اَلْإِكْسِير (al-ʔiksīr, “philosopher's stone”), from Ancient Greek ξηρίον (xēríon, “powder for drying wounds”), from ξηρός (xērós, “dry”).

ex.en: The old man claimed he had found the elixir of life.
ex.ja: その老人は不老不死の霊薬を見つけたと言い張った。

note.ja: アラビア語 al-iksīr（錬金術の薬）から。ギリシャ語 xērion（乾いた粉薬）。「霊薬」。

en: The final stage of a game of chess, when there are few pieces left.
The final stage of a game of bridge, when there are few cards left.

ex.en: The negotiations are entering the endgame.
ex.ja: 交渉は最終段階に入りつつある。

note.ja: end（終わり）+ game（試合）。チェスの「終盤戦」→「最終段階」。

en: An illuminating realization or discovery, often resulting in a personal feeling of elation, awe, or wonder.

English Epiphany (of Christ) since the 14th century, generic use since the 17th century.

ex.en: She had an epiphany about her career.
ex.ja: 彼女は自分の仕事についてふと悟った。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 epiphaneia（出現）から。epi（上に）+ phainein（現れる）。神の出現 →「ひらめき」。phenomenon と同じ。

ex.ja: アイライナー貸してもらえないかな？

en: A fictitious narrative intended to enforce some useful truth or precept, usually with animals, etc. as characters; an apologue. Prototypi…
Any story told to excite wonder; common talk; the theme of talk.

fable.ety: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French fable, from Latin fābula, from fārī (“to speak, say”) + -bula (“instrumental suffix”). See ban, and compare fabulous, fame. Doublet of fabula.

ex.en: The following passage was quoted from a well-known fable.
ex.ja: 次の一節はある有名な寓話から引用したものです。

ex.en: The following passage is a quotation from a well-known fable.
ex.ja: 次の一節はある有名な寓話から引用したものです。

ex.en: In Aesop's Fables is a story called "Sour Grapes".
ex.ja: イソップ童話に『すっぱい葡萄』という話があります。

note.ja: ラテン語 fabula（話）から。fari（話す）。「寓話」。fabulous、fame、fate と同じ語源。

en: Wood intended to be burned, typically for heat.

firewood.ety: From Middle English ferwode, fyrewoode, equivalent to fire + wood.

ex.en: He broke up the chair for firewood.
ex.ja: 彼は椅子を叩き壊して薪にした。

ex.en: He set up a bundle of firewood.
ex.ja: 彼は、まきを束ねた。

ex.en: Tom is chopping firewood.
ex.ja: トムは薪割りしてるよ。

note.ja: fire（火）+ wood（木）。「まき」。

en: A hill at the base of a mountain or mountain range.

foothill.ety:

From foot + hill.

ex.en: The village lies in the foothills of the Alps.
ex.ja: その村はアルプスのふもとの丘陵地帯にある。

note.ja: foot（ふもと）+ hill（丘）。「ふもとの丘」。

en: The ability, or the due use of one's ability, to foresee or prepare wisely for the future.
The ability to foresee future events in a supernatural or paranormal way, such as psychically.

foresight.ety: From Middle English forsight, forsyght, forsichte (since 14th c.), a calque of Latin providentia. By surface analysis, fore- + sight. Compare Scots foresicht, Saterland Frisian Foarsicht, archaic Dutch voorzicht (now voorzichtigheid), German Vorsicht (all “caution, foresight”).

ex.en: They blamed me for my lack of foresight.
ex.ja: 彼らは見通しが甘かったといって私を責めた。

ex.en: Clear foresight contributed greatly to his success.
ex.ja: 彼の成功には明確な見通しが非常に役立った。

ex.en: He congratulates himself on his foresight.
ex.ja: 彼は彼の洞察力を得意に思っている。

note.ja: fore（前もって）+ sight（見ること）。「先見の明」。hindsight（あと知恵）の対。

en: Deserted; abandoned.
Helpless.

ex.en: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
ex.ja: 神よ、神よ、なぜ私を見捨てられたか？

note.ja: forsake（見捨てる）の過去分詞。for（完全に）+ sake（争う）。「見捨てられた」。

en: One who reduces religion to strict interpretation of core or original texts.
A trader who trades on the financial fundamentals of the companies involved, as opposed to a chartist or technician.

fundamentalist.ety: From fundamental + -ist, after a book series called “The Fundamentals: A Testimony to the Truth“ (1910).

ex.en: The group has fundamentalist beliefs.
ex.ja: その集団は原理主義的な信念を持っている。

note.ja: fundamental（根本的な）+ -ist。根本の教えに固執する人 →「原理主義者」。

en: A horse which is hired out.
In full hackney carriage, hackney coach: a horse-drawn carriage which is hired out.
To make (something) uninteresting and unoriginal through frequent repetition; to make (something) trite.

hackney.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English hakeney (“small horse, often hired out”), probably from Hakeneia, Hakeneye (“Hackney, formerly a village in Middlesex and now a borough of London, England, in the United Kingdom”) (as the surrounding meadows were used for grazing horses before sale; whence Old French haquenée (“ambling mare for ladies”), Latinized in England to hakeneius), from Old English *Hacan īeġ (“Haca’s Island”, literally “Hook’s Island”).
The adjective and verb are derived from the noun.

ex.en: A hackney carriage waited outside the hotel.
ex.ja: ホテルの外で貸し馬車が待っていた。

note.ja: ロンドン近郊の地名 Hackney とされる。そこで飼われていた馬 →「貸し馬」→ 使い古された →「陳腐な（hackneyed）」。hack（ありふれた作家）と同じ。

en: One of the great tendons situated in each side of the ham, or space back of the knee, and connected with the muscles of the back of the t…
The biceps femoris, semimembranosus, and semitendinosus muscles.
To lame or disable by cutting the tendons of the ham or knee; to hough.
To cripple; to incapacitate; to disable.

hamstring.ety: From ham (“region back of the knee joint”) + string.

ex.en: He pulled a hamstring during the race.
ex.ja: 彼はレース中にハムストリングを痛めた。

note.ja: ham（膝の裏）+ string（腱）。「膝の裏の腱」→ 腱を切って動けなくする →「無力にする」。

The U shape of a horseshoe.
To apply horseshoes to (a horse).

en: A cut, especially one made by a scalpel or similar medical tool in the context of surgical operation; the scar resulting from such a cut.
The act of cutting into a substance.

incision.ety: From Middle English inscicioun, from Middle French incision, from Late Latin incisiō from the verb incidō (“to cut into”) + action noun suffix -iō.

ex.en: The surgeon made a small incision.
ex.ja: 外科医は小さく切開した。

note.ja: ラテン語 incisio（切り込み）から。in + caedere（切る）。「切開」。decide、precise と同じ cis。

en: Not distinguishable; not capable of being perceived, known, or discriminated as separate and distinct
Not capable of being perceived or known.
Any of a set of things that cannot be distinguished.

ex.en: The twins are indistinguishable from each other.
ex.ja: その双子は見分けがつかない。

note.ja: in + distinguish + -able。「区別できない」。

en: To introduce (something) as a reasoned conclusion; to conclude by reasoning or deduction, as from premises or evidence.
To lead to (something) as a consequence; to imply.

infer.ety: From Latin inferō, from Latin in- (“in, at, on; into”) + Latin ferō (“bear, carry; suffer”) (cognate to Old English beran, whence English bear), from Proto-Italic *ferō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰéreti (“to bear, carry”), from the root *bʰer-. Literally “carry forward”, equivalent to “bear in”, as in concluding from a premise. Doublet of inbear.

ex.en: What do you infer from her strange behavior?
ex.ja: 彼女の異常なふるまいから何を推測しますか。

ex.en: She inferred from his silence that he was angry.
ex.ja: 彼が黙っていたので、彼女は怒っているのだと思った。

ex.en: I inferred from her expression that she was angry.
ex.ja: 彼女の表情から怒っているのを察した。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ fer（運ぶ）。（結論を）中へ運び込む →「推論する・推測する」。inference（推論）。

en: A patient whose treatment requires at least one night's residence in a hospital; a hospitalized patient.
Of treatment, requiring at least one night's residence in a hospital.

ex.en: He was treated as an inpatient for a week.
ex.ja: 彼は１週間入院して治療を受けた。

note.ja: in（中の）+ patient（患者）。「入院患者」。outpatient の対。impatient（いらいらした）と区別。

Restricted to participants who have been invited.
An event, especially a tournament, that is restricted to invited participants

en: A house or shelter for a dog.
A facility at which dogs are reared or boarded.
To house or board a dog (or less commonly another animal).
To lie or lodge; to dwell, as a dog or a fox.

ex.en: It took me five hours to make this kennel.
ex.ja: この犬小屋を作るのに五時間かかった。

ex.en: He made a kennel with his son on Sunday.
ex.ja: 彼は日曜日に息子といっしょに犬小屋を作った。

ex.en: Our dog is in the kennel.
ex.ja: うちの犬は犬小屋にいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 canis（犬）から古フランス語を経た語。「犬小屋」。canine と同じ。

en: A member of an ethnolinguistic group that constitutes most of the population of Cambodia.
Of or pertaining to the Khmer people or their language.

Khmer.ety: From the French romanization of Khmer ខ្មែរ (khmae).

ex.en: Angkor Wat was built by the Khmer.
ex.ja: アンコールワットはクメール人によって建てられた。

note.ja: カンボジアの主要民族の名前。

en: A type of beer, brewed using a bottom-fermenting yeast.
To store (lager beer) at a low temperature for maturing and clarification.

lager.ety: From German Lagerbier (“beer made for storing”), from Lager (“store”). Cognate with native English lair.

ex.en: I'd like a lager.
ex.ja: ラガーがいいな。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Lagerbier（貯蔵ビール）から。Lager（貯蔵所）。低温で貯蔵して造ることから。

en: Sense of revulsion, distaste, detestation, extreme hatred or dislike.

loathing.ety: From the verb loathe. Compare loathsome.

ex.en: He felt a deep loathing for war.
ex.ja: 彼は戦争に深い嫌悪を感じていた。

note.ja: loathe（ひどく嫌う）+ -ing。古英語 lāth（憎い）。「嫌悪」。

en: A person who is loyal to a cause, generally used as a political affiliation.

loyalist.ety: From loyal + -ist. Piecewise doublet of legalist.

ex.en: What do you think you're doing letting the loyalists into the castle?
ex.ja: 官軍に入城を許すとはどういう了見だ。

note.ja: loyal + -ist。「忠誠派」。

en: The state or condition of being a human being.
The state or condition of being a man, as contrasted with being a boy, woman, girl, or nonbinary.

manhood.ety: From Middle English manhode, also manhede (> obsolete English manhead), equivalent to man + -hood. Cognate with Middle Dutch manheit (“manhood”), Middle Low German manheit (whence German Low German Mannheit (“manhood”)), German Mannheit (“manhood”).

ex.en: He is now in the prime of manhood.
ex.ja: 彼は今男盛りだ。

ex.en: Most athletes are at their best during their early manhood.
ex.ja: 多くの運動選手は青年時代に盛りを極める。

ex.en: He is approaching manhood.
ex.ja: 彼は大人になりつつある。

note.ja: man + -hood。「成年男子であること・男らしさ」。

en: The condition of a martyr; the death or suffering of a martyr; the death or suffering on account of adherence to the Christian faith, or …
Extreme suffering, affliction; torment; torture, especially without reason.

martyrdom.ety: From Middle English martyrdome, martirdom, marterdom, from Old English martyrdōm (“martyrdom”), corresponding to martyr + -dom. Cognate with German Märtyrertum (“martyrdom”), Danish martyrdom (“martyrdom”), Swedish martyrdom (“martyrdom”), Norwegian martyrdom (“martyrdom”).

ex.en: The saint's martyrdom is remembered every year.
ex.ja: その聖人の殉教は毎年追悼されている。

note.ja: martyr（殉教者）+ -dom。ギリシャ語 martys（証人）。「信仰を証しして死ぬこと」→「殉教」。

The final menstrual period of a woman after which ovulation no longer occurs.

ex.en: Women usually reach menopause around fifty.
ex.ja: 女性はふつう５０歳前後で更年期を迎える。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 mēn（月）+ pausis（停止）。「月のものが止まること」→「閉経」。month と同系、pause と同じ。

en: The primary circuit board of a personal computer, containing the circuitry for the central processing unit, keyboard, mouse and monitor, …

motherboard.ety: Compound of mother + board. Attested since 1965.

ex.en: The motherboard of the computer was damaged.
ex.ja: コンピューターのマザーボードが壊れた。

note.ja: mother（母）+ board（基板）。ほかの基板を差し込む親基板。

en: Having undergone mutilation

ex.en: The old book was badly mutilated.
ex.ja: その古い本はひどく傷んでいた。

note.ja: mutilate（切断する）+ -ed。mutilation と同じ。
